evidence: Worksheet title: 'Cuadro N° 60c — Tipo de cambio real bilateral — (enero 1995 = 100)'. The published title states the base explicitly, so the five columns are index numbers, not prices of foreign currency. Control case: CUADRO 60b publishes the same series under the same labels and the same identity hashes ('economic_annex:cuadro_60b:293a83a82f814b7fc49afadc' for IPC) already coded unit 'index', unit_code INDEX, currency null. The observed range 100.00-659.46 is an index level, and the value is exactly 100.00 at the stated base. The defect is worksheet-level unit inheritance: every column on 60c took the sheet default PYG_per_USD. Audit: revisiones/EMPIRICAL_READINESS_2026-09-03.md ER-01.

Worksheet title: 'Cuadro N° 60a — Tipo de cambio nominal del guarani'. The table quotes the guarani against four currencies in four columns and the parser gave all four the sheet default PYG_per_USD; only the 'USD 1/' column can have a dollar denominator. This column is the euro. Confirmed against the dollar column on the same rows: 2024-01 euro 7945.71 with USD 7283.00 implies EUR/USD 1.091, and 2026-07 euro 6912.13 with USD 6049.62 implies 1.143 -- both the prevailing cross rates. The same quotation is already coded PYG_PER_EUR on exchange_rates 'EURO Prom' and 'EURO Fin Mes'. Audit: revisiones/EMPIRICAL_READINESS_2026-09-03.md ER-01.

Worksheet title: 'Cuadro N° 60a — Tipo de cambio nominal del guarani'. This column is the Argentine peso, not the US dollar. Confirmed against the dollar column on the same rows: 2024-01 peso 8.90 with USD 7283.00 implies ARS/USD 818, and 2026-07 peso 4.07 with USD 6049.62 implies 1486 -- the Argentine peso's path over that window. The companion table CUADRO 60c publishes 'TCR Arg' for the same counterpart, and exchange_rates 'PESO Fin Mes' already codes this quotation PYG_PER_ARS. The 8.90-to-4.07 decline is Argentine inflation, not a unit change, and needs no regime split. Audit: revisiones/EMPIRICAL_READINESS_2026-09-03.md ER-01.
